svg.title: Five Core Seats, Two Explicit Scale Additions
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-five-to-seven-person-pod; chart type: org_architecture; title: Five Core Seats, Two Explicit Scale Additions; subtitle: Separate commercial ownership, engineering, quality, and bounded support.; chapter number: 11; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Each numeric value is one person-slot, not one full-time equivalent. The first five seats form the Conservative and Base pod: 2 FT + 3 C. Activate the final two seats only for the Scaled pod: 3 FT + 4 C.; caption: Canonical annual revenue / margin / owner net profit: Conservative $100,000 / 20% / $20,000; Base $550,000 / 30.0% / $165,000; Scaled $1,000,000 / 40% / $400,000. Revenue per person-slot is $20,000, $110,000, and approximately $142,857 respectively; these are not revenue-per-full-time-equivalent measures.; stages: label: FT 1: commercial and product lead; value: Core seat owning scope, pricing, and client decisions; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own discovery, signed statements of work, change pricing, and renewal evidence. Resolve scope conflicts without allowing unpaid features to enter the engineering queue.; label: FT 2: technical delivery lead; value: Core seat owning architecture, access, and production release; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own integration boundaries, credential design, evaluation thresholds, and rollback readiness. Review contractor changes and maintain the deployable reference implementation.; label: C 1: integration engineer; value: Core contractor building connectors and reliable workflow execution; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Implement API mappings, retries, idempotency, and queue handling within the purchased scope. Submit versioned changes with reproducible tests and document external API limits.; label: C 2: evaluation specialist; value: Core contractor testing quality, permissions, and adversarial inputs; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Maintain held-out fixtures, score output defects, and test retrieval isolation. Report failed cases separately from aggregate accuracy so severe exceptions remain visible.; label: C 3: workflow and support specialist; value: Core contractor documenting handoffs and handling bounded support; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Map operator procedures, prepare training material, and triage support requests. Escalate quality regressions to the technical lead and route enhancement requests into priced change work.; label: FT 3: scaled service operations lead; value: Scaled-only addition managing capacity, incidents, and renewal readiness; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Join when contracted workload supports a dedicated operations seat. Own service calendars, client reporting, incident coordination, and retainer capacity rather than duplicating the sales role.; label: C 4: scaled implementation specialist; value: Scaled-only addition expanding delivery capacity for repeatable packages; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Take repeatable connector or migration work from the technical lead. Activate against signed delivery backlog; preserve the same tests and documentation rather than creating a separate custom-service line.
